original_test_intent: Determine whether the authorized Chassis Power resource advertises a documented PowerSupplyReset capability and capture its vendor-defined metadata without invoking it; the current source cannot safely define a request to the action target.
original_method: Keep the case blocked, read only the parent Power resource's Actions metadata if approved, and require a corrected vendor-backed testcase with exact PSU/reset semantics before any action-target request is constructed.
manual_activity: The platform power/firmware owner must decide capability discovery versus actual PSU reset, identify the exact supply/power domain and redundancy state, and provide the vendor verb, payload, expected response, workload impact and recovery plan.
required_inputs: Authorized Chassis and Power resource links
Documented action target, method and payload
Exact PSU or power-domain selection semantics
OOB recovery and acceptable post-reset state
Trusted credential/certificate and preserved evidence plan
safety_requirements: Do not call the malformed or normalized action target
Do not change GET to POST
Do not invent a PSU selector or payload
No PSU cycle or chassis power transition
Require separate outage approval for any future invocation
agent_execution_scope: Read only the parent Power resource if approved
Compare advertised target/parameters with vendor specification
Prove no action request or power transition occurred
engineer_actions: Correct the testcase and supply authoritative PowerSupplyReset semantics
Approve PSU/redundancy/workload impact and recovery for any separate invocation

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It must not run: DeepSeek silently removes the source's path space but GET still has no documented action contract, ipmitool is unrelated, and changing to an invocation could cycle an unspecified supply or power domain.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: BLOCKED. At most, securely GET the authorized parent Power resource and inspect its Actions metadata; never call PowerSupplyReset until the vendor contract, exact PSU scope, redundancy impact, payload, acceptance and recovery are separately approved.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The PowerSupplyReset name and 15/10 timing remain only as unresolved facts; ChassisId, supply, method, payload, expected transition and recovery are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Separate read-only capability discovery from a future controlled PSU-reset experiment, whose power-domain target, redundancy prerequisites, workload outage envelope and recovery evidence are explicitly defined.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Prevents a malformed GET from being normalized into an executable power action or a likely action failure from being mistaken for capability evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Parent Power metadata can show an advertised action but cannot prove invocation authorization, selected supply, failover behavior, service continuity or recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A reset may drop a rail, defeat redundancy, brown out the chassis or strand the BMC depending on vendor semantics; OOB recovery may itself share the affected power path.

project_override_considerations: No Redfish SDK, vendor utility or ipmitool command may invoke a PSU reset under this record. While blocked, tooling is limited to parent Power metadata reads; invocation needs a new approved contract.
expected_evidence: Secure parent Power response with redacted Actions metadata
Advertised action target/parameters and malformed-source-path analysis
PSU/redundancy/power-domain impact and recovery gap report
Preserved PSU telemetry, BMC/SEL/OS and workload state evidence

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The testcase names a PowerSupplyReset action but uses GET on a malformed action-target URI and defines no readable representation, PSU selector, payload, expected transition or recovery. If invocation is intended, the required state-changing contract is absent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Neither source nor references establish a safe GET contract or the target supply/power-domain semantics. Correcting the request could cause a disruptive power action, so vendor specification and a corrected, separately approved safety contract are indispensable.

review_improvement: Blocks the silently normalized action URI and defines the PSU scope, redundancy, workload-impact and recovery evidence that a legitimate PowerSupplyReset test would require.
independent_technical_reasoning: A PowerSupplyReset action may target one replaceable supply, a logical power subsystem or an OEM controller; without vendor semantics, its blast radius cannot be bounded. The embedded path space is an additional source defect, but removing it does not make GET meaningful. A guessed POST could interrupt power, and even redundant hardware may not preserve service if feeds or firmware dependencies are shared. Only parent Actions metadata is safe until the exact target, payload, expected transition and independent recovery are documented.
